verification.staticChecks: Scoped ESLint and Prettier passed. Final Web and Server typechecks passed. Earlier test-only Server typing errors and a focus-effect lint violation were corrected and the affected checks passed afterward. No local full-repository aggregate check was run.
verification.build: The initial shared server/web/quant-engine Docker build passed. Actual blank-name/degraded-state findings required an affected server/web rebuild; the browser focus finding required the final Web target build. The final Web target also compiled both Node applications through the existing shared stage. The running server and quant-engine images were reused where their executed source, dependencies and configuration were unchanged; unrelated UI changes and documentation do not require rebuilding those runtimes.

browser.actual: Authenticated localhost application loaded the existing durable account through the real server/engine chain. Manual refresh retained the original cash 100000 CNY, zero positions, two ledger events and ledger time displayed as 2026/09/05 14:14:36 in Asia/Shanghai. No account create or simulate request was sent to the real ledger.
browser.isolated: A temporary loopback-only proxy served synthetic auth/workspace responses and read-only static assets. All upstream API access was blocked; POST create was held only in process, first returned 503 and then succeeded. Empty, invalid, cancel/reopen, native disabled/progress, failure input retention, retry key/payload identity and success close/refresh were verified. It did not prove a newly created real journal command; durable replay was verified separately against existing state.
browser.layout: Label/input gaps were 8px. At a 390px viewport the final dark Dialog had client/scroll width 390px with readable dark fields; the account view had no horizontal overflow. The viewport was reset; synthetic tab and process were closed.
browser.screenshot: The actual authenticated account page, ledger timestamp, balances, empty holdings and simulation boundaries were inspected and saved in ignored local work.
browser.keyboardRefresh: Enter on the actual refresh button completed; the returned connected button was active and matched :focus-visible.

persistence.beforeAfterRestart: Account fingerprint, cash, NAV, positions, event count and journal bytes/hash were identical before and after one quant-engine restart. Final journal bytes/hash also matched the original pre-start baseline after all browser tests.
persistence.recoveryScope: Existing command-journal replay only; no schema/storage/procedure change or repeated backup-restore drill.

Only that test expectation was updated; 17 App tests and scoped lint/format then passed. No application or runtime source changed, so build, browser and independent-review evidence is reused.

localRuntime.containers: Web, server and quant-engine healthy; existing databases, workers and their state preserved. No collection run, migration or production deployment.

knownLimits: Single local administrator, single engine instance and one simulation account; no account reset/delete, multi-account isolation, order/intent entry, simulated fills, automatic valuations, PnL or real-broker capability is delivered.
Amounts are historical simulation ledger values and position costs, independent of the global historical quote context; they are not real funds or current executable prices.
The existing account has no holdings; non-empty, malformed, error/forbidden and degraded states are covered by contract-compatible tests rather than writes to the real journal.

No Python/accounting/schema/API contract/dependency/auth model changes. The development engine retains legacy simulation behavior outside the v1 product profile. This accepts only the P6-N08 release slice, not full P6-N08, Phase 6 endurance/exit, Phase 7 or production readiness.
